item.title: Installation
item.description:
Quick Reference

Use this section as an on-site checklist. For detailed instructions, continue to the relevant installation method below.

Critical Placement Rules

These rules are mandatory for all doorframe installations. Violating any rule will degrade counting accuracy or cause false counts.

  1. Maximum 1 cm from doorframe edge — The sensor must be flush with the bottom edge of the doorframe. A gap larger than 1 cm shifts the detection zone.
  2. Never install on the door-swing side — Mount the sensor on the opposite side from where the door opens. Door movement triggers false counts.
  3. Ceiling: minimum 1 meter from obstructions — When ceiling-mounted, the sensor must be at least 1 meter from any doorframe, wall, or beam.

item.title: Operation
item.description:
How 3-PIR Detection Works

Patented Triple Passive Infrared Technology

The Haltian ENTRYWAY uses three Passive Infrared (PIR) sensors in a patented configuration to detect people moving through doorways.

Detection principle:

  1. Three PIR beams: Sensor has three parallel PIR detection zones across passageway
  2. Heat detection: PIR sensors detect infrared radiation (heat) emitted by human bodies
  3. Sequential triggering: Person walking through triggers beams sequentially (Beam 1 → Beam 2 → Beam 3)
  4. Direction determination: Order of beam triggering determines direction (entry vs. exit)
  5. Count increment: Entry or exit counter increments

PIR Beam Configuration

  • Three parallel beams: Spaced to cover passageway width (up to 1600mm)
  • Horizontal detection zones: Beams oriented across passageway (perpendicular to traffic flow)
  • Thermal sensitivity: Detects difference between body heat (~36-37°C) and ambient temperature

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
Configuration Overview

Haltian ENTRYWAY sensors are remotely configurable via Haltian IoT. This allows adjusting key parameters without physical access to the sensor.

Key configurable parameters:

  • Entry direction: Which side is “entry” vs. “exit”
  • Measurement interval: How often sensor reports during active period
  • Reporting interval (idle): How often sensor reports when no movement detected
Note

Configuration changes require access to Haltian IoT. Contact Haltian support if you need assistance with remote configuration.

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
This FAQ answers common questions about Haltian ENTRYWAY. For step-by-step diagnosis of counting, connectivity, and battery issues, see Troubleshooting.

Product Basics

What is Haltian ENTRYWAY?

Haltian ENTRYWAY is a wireless, privacy-first people-counting sensor based on patented bi-directional 3-PIR detection. It counts directional movement through doorways and passages, reporting entries and exits without cameras or personal data collection.

How is ENTRYWAY different from a Presence sensor?

ENTRYWAY measures directional movement: how many people enter and exit a space. A Presence sensor reports binary occupancy: whether a space is occupied or unoccupied.
